title: the voyage and the board's engine badge show each crewman's real vendor and model, never the config rule 'opposite-of-host'
acceptance:
Why. On 2026-10-05 the captain saw every sailor and reviewer in the 2.5D voyage labelled 'opposite-of-host' instead of the vendor and model actually running ("我要確切的模型"). The per-crewman values already exist in `/api/state` as `vendor`, `model`, `model_source`, `model_requested` and `model_mismatch` (board/server.ts:1197-1202); for example `worker-shira-t189-r3` is `codex` / `gpt-6-astra`. Two places ignore them:
- BoardSource sets every crewman's `vendor` to `s.engine?.vendor` (games/voyage-2d/src/board-source.js:54), which is config.yaml's top-level `vendor:`, now the rule `opposite-of-host` (config.yaml:9). The HUD shows only that value and no model (games/voyage-2d/src/hud.js:429, :436).
- The board's engine badge shows the same raw value (board/public/index.html:476-483, from `engine()` at board/server.ts:316-333).

Voyage mapping. BoardSource already spreads each crew row (`...c`, board-source.js:50) and then overwrites `model` with the sprite key; that sprite `model` stays exactly as is, because world.js:336 reads it. BoardSource sets these fields from the crewman's own row and never from `s.engine`:
- `vendor` ← `c.vendor`
- `llm` ← `c.model`
- `llm_source` ← `c.model_source`
- `llm_mismatch` ← `c.model_mismatch`
- `llm_requested` ← `c.model_requested`

HUD labels. The zh locales label vendor as 模型 today (hud.js:56, :78), which would clash with a model field. Change them as follows:
- zh-TW: vendor becomes 供應商; a new `llm` label is 模型.
- zh-CN: vendor becomes 供应商 (hud.js keeps its own zh-CN block at :78, so i18n/tw2cn.tsv is not involved); `llm` is 模型.
- en: `llm` is "Model".
The HUD's 'requested' mark and mismatch warning use new keys in all three `f:`/text blocks; `stringKeys()` (hud.js:149) picks them up for tests/mod.test.mjs.

HUD fields and roster per mode.
- Live mode: `crewFields` (hud.js:424-430) returns, in order, name, role, project, task, round, pr, state, activity, vendor, llm. The llm cell shows `llm` plus the 'requested' mark while `llm_source` is `requested`, or the mismatch warning text when `llm_mismatch` is true, or the existing 'none' when absent.
- Playground mode: unchanged, including `rank` and the combined vendor strings from main.js:168 (out of scope), still 10 columns as tests/browser.test.mjs:551 and :531 assert.
- `rosterHtml` (hud.js:459) picks its header list per mode: the live list is the live `crewFields` keys (10 columns, no rank); the playground list is today's 10 keys. Every row then has exactly as many cells as headers in both modes.

Badge resolution. `engine()` resolves `opposite-of-host` exactly as the launcher's `fm_role_vendor` does (bin/fm-config.sh:503-517):
- Host: the `harness` field of `stateDir(P)/session/host.json`, falling back to `<engine>/state/session/host.json`. P is `process.env.FM_PROJECT || defaultProject()`. This is the same lookup and project `firstmateHost` uses (board/server.ts:597-610, :1143), and it mirrors `fm_host_harness` (bin/fm-config.sh:467-474).
- Mapping: host claude → codex; codex → claude; anything else, including no record → the first `fallback:` entry of config.yaml, or `mock` if there is none.
- The top-level vendor and `reviewer.vendor` are each resolved when they are the rule. With no reviewer block, `reviewer` stays null and `cross` stays false, as today (tests/board-readiness.test.sh:61-62). This deliberately keeps the badge's existing reviewer semantics.
- Return shape: `{vendor, reviewer, cross, rule, reviewer_rule, host}`. `vendor` and `reviewer` are the resolved names. `rule` and `reviewer_rule` are the raw config value when it was a rule, otherwise null. `host` is the harness read, or null. `cross` compares the resolved names.

Badge display. When no crew is aboard, the badge shows the resolved `vendor`, marked `⇄ reviewer` when `cross`, as today. When `rule` is set, the tooltip appends `rule (host → vendor)` using the raw identifiers, for example `opposite-of-host (claude → codex)`, with `?` for a null host. It uses only the existing `engine` and `crossVendor` strings plus these identifiers, so no new i18n key is needed and i18n/*.json stays out of scope. A plain vendor name renders exactly as today.

Design. §8's "Engine badge (V7)" paragraph (design/design.md:1590-1593) is amended in place. The header shows the top-level vendor resolved as the launcher would: a rule such as `opposite-of-host` is resolved from the recorded host, and the rule is shown in the tooltip. Crew vendor and model always come from the run's identity, in the board and in the voyage. No other section changes.
Migration. Nothing stored changes; this is display only. Plain-vendor configs keep their current output.

Tests (fail first):
- BoardSource (games/voyage-2d/tests/board-source.test.mjs): two crew rows with different vendors and models. Each crewman's `vendor`, `llm`, `llm_source` and `llm_mismatch` come from its own row, the sprite `model` is unchanged, and `s.engine.vendor` never appears.
- HUD (`crewFields` called directly): live rows have 10 cells ending vendor, llm; the 'requested' mark and the mismatch warning show; zh-TW and zh-CN vendor labels are 供應商 and 供应商 and the llm label is 模型; the playground crewFields still has 10 cells including rank; the live and playground rosterHtml header counts equal their row cell counts.
- Board (tests/board-readiness.test.sh additions): with no crew, config `vendor: opposite-of-host` and host.json harness claude, `.engine` is vendor codex, rule opposite-of-host, host claude; with harness codex, vendor claude; with no host record, vendor is the first fallback entry, or mock with no fallback; a project-state host.json wins over the engine's; with `reviewer.vendor: opposite-of-host`, reviewer resolves and `cross` compares resolved names.
- Regressions named and kept passing unchanged: tests/board-readiness.test.sh:45-62 (plain vendors, per-request read, no reviewer block gives null), tests/e2e/board-layout.spec.ts:34-39, tests/e2e/board-crew.spec.ts:185-186 (live badge).
- Page: an e2e or unit check that the tooltip contains `opposite-of-host (claude → codex)` for the rule case.
Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Workers do not run the suites.

Mirror doc. games/voyage-2d/docs/interface.md states that a crewman's vendor comes from the board's engine value. It is updated in the same change: vendor and model come from each crewman's own crew row, and `model` stays the sprite key.
